nv_brown_warm_up_boulder.blurb: A single free-standing block among the Black Velvet Canyon boulders in Red Rock, a short wander off the main canyon trail. Four faces of mostly square, vertical, desert-varnished sandstone hold 18 problems, which makes it the busiest stop of its group. The spread is friendly: several problems sit at VB to V1, a handful more at V2 and V3, and just one reaches V5. Its standouts are moderate crack and face lines around V2 and V3. It suits a warm-up or a quick stop on the way in or out of the canyon, rather than a full day of hard bouldering.

nv_compton_cave_the.blurb: A big steep cave at the far end of The Hood, the limestone sport cliff high on Mount Charleston in the Spring Mountains. Eighteen bolted routes cover a hard range: one around 5.11, a few at 5.12, and most of the rest from 5.13 into 5.14, with the toughest lines on the left wall. Climbing here is overhanging and powerful, on smooth pocketed stone. The recesses of the cave and nearby pines give shade, and the altitude keeps it cooler than the valley below. This is a destination for strong sport climbers, not a place for moderates or beginners.

nv_mary_jane_cliff.blurb: A shady sport crag in Kyle Canyon on Mount Charleston, a cool retreat from summer heat in the Las Vegas valley. The approach is short, only a few minutes up the canyon trail from the trailhead, ending at a cliff above the wash on the southwest side. Eighteen bolted routes run from about 5.8 to 5.13, with the bulk of them at 5.11 and a few easier and harder ones either side. The stone is a mix of gray slabby sections and steeper orange rock, and the best-known line follows a pocketed corner. Expect sustained climbing in the 5.11 range rather than a beginner crag.

nv_cheap_beer_crag.blurb: A small limestone sport cliff on the east side of Lone Mountain, inside the Las Vegas valley. It sits a short distance up the slope from Urban Crag, and is reached by walking along the base of the cliff past that crag. Eighteen bolted routes range from about 5.6 to 5.11, with most of them clustered around 5.10 and a few easier warm-ups below. There is a cave area and a chert wall further uphill. The cliff is sheltered and catches good sun, so it works well on cold days and as a fast-drying backup when Red Rock is wet.

nv_dinosaur_rock.blurb: A small roadside crag just south of Carson City beside Clear Creek, which shades it in summer while the east-side climbs catch sun for most of the day. Eighteen routes mix trad and sport, mostly trad, from about 5.6 up to 5.12, with a good number of easy and moderate lines at 5.6 to 5.9. Several routes can be set up as top-ropes, so it is often used for learning to lead and place gear. The rock is weathered but solid, and the walls are short. Crowds are usually light, and late spring through early fall is the comfortable window.

nv_illusion_crags.blurb: A quiet cluster of small cliffs in the southern outcrops of Red Rock, well away from the busy canyons. All 18 routes are single-pitch trad, and most are bolt-free, so bring a full rack. The sandstone spread is mostly moderate: eight routes at 5.7, several at 5.8 and 5.9, a single easier one near 5.6, and two at 5.11. Left-side climbs generally have walk-offs, while longer lines on the main east-facing face are descended by rappel. Crowds are usually thin, which suits climbers who want an uncrowded moderate trad day.
